title: Ecosystem Disturbance and Recovery Review Test
description: Use before-and-after data, food webs, and comparison sites to explain ecosystem responses to disturbance and evaluate recovery.

questions.prompt: A windstorm opens gaps while leaving soil intact. Which first prediction is most reasonable?
questions.questionText: A windstorm opens gaps while leaving soil intact. Which first prediction is most reasonable?
options: Every gap must begin as bare rock.
All original tree species return before any small plants.
Light and surviving plant material may support a changed mix of seedlings.
The soil has no effect on what establishes.
questions.correctAnswer: Light and surviving plant material may support a changed mix of seedlings.
questions.explanation: Canopy gaps change conditions while leaving biological resources that influence regrowth.

questions.prompt: An abandoned paved area has almost no soil; a nearby unmown lawn retains soil. Why might their recovery differ?
questions.questionText: An abandoned paved area has almost no soil; a nearby unmown lawn retains soil. Why might their recovery differ?
options: They must follow an identical timeline because both are unused.
The paved area needs no water because it has no soil.
They begin with different substrates and surviving organisms.
The lawn's plants must all become trees.
questions.correctAnswer: They begin with different substrates and surviving organisms.
questions.explanation: Starting conditions shape pathways and rates of community change.

questions.prompt: After a spill, plant counts are 50 before, 15 after one week, and 35 after one year. How many plants below baseline is the final count?
questions.questionText: After a spill, plant counts are 50 before, 15 after one week, and 35 after one year. How many plants below baseline is the final count?
options: 15 plants.
20 plants.
35 plants.
50 plants.
questions.explanation: The final count is 50 - 35 = 15 below baseline; the gain since week one is a different quantity.

questions.prompt: A mowed field stays dominated by short grasses. What change could permit taller plants to establish, if seeds and resources are available?
questions.questionText: A mowed field stays dominated by short grasses. What change could permit taller plants to establish, if seeds and resources are available?
options: Mowing more often at the same height.
Removing every nearby seed source.
Longer intervals between mowing.
Reducing water below the plants' needs.
questions.explanation: Less frequent disturbance gives taller plants time to establish under suitable conditions.

questions.prompt: Two recovering sites both have 60% plant cover. What additional result would show they are biologically different?
questions.questionText: Two recovering sites both have 60% plant cover. What additional result would show they are biologically different?
options: Both have the same sampled area.
One has six native species; the other is dominated by one introduced species.
Both were measured on the same date.
Both used the same cover method.
questions.correctAnswer: One has six native species; the other is dominated by one introduced species.
questions.explanation: Equal cover can hide important differences in species composition.

questions.prompt: A restored stream's plants return before fish counts recover. Which explanation is plausible?
questions.questionText: A restored stream's plants return before fish counts recover. Which explanation is plausible?
options: Returning plants guarantee instant fish recovery.
Fish abundance must always recover before plant cover.
Delayed fish recovery proves the plant measurements false.
Food, shelter, access, or water conditions may still limit fish.
questions.correctAnswer: Food, shelter, access, or water conditions may still limit fish.
questions.explanation: Interacting populations can respond at different rates and have different limiting factors.

questions.prompt: A diagram says fewer flowers -> fewer insects -> fewer insect-eating birds. Which arrow describes an indirect effect of flower loss?
questions.questionText: A diagram says fewer flowers -> fewer insects -> fewer insect-eating birds. Which arrow describes an indirect effect of flower loss?
options: The immediate loss of flowers itself.
A bird directly eating a flower in this model.
The pathway from flowers through insects to birds.
A flower turning into a bird.
questions.correctAnswer: The pathway from flowers through insects to birds.
questions.explanation: The bird effect is mediated through the insect food supply.

questions.prompt: A protected site increases from 20 to 45 plants; a matched open site increases from 20 to 40. What is the difference between their increases?
questions.questionText: A protected site increases from 20 to 45 plants; a matched open site increases from 20 to 40. What is the difference between their increases?
options: 25 plants.
40 plants.
65 plants.
5 plants.
questions.explanation: The gains are 25 and 20, a difference of 5; this is smaller than the protected site's total gain.

questions.prompt: What would weaken a claim that planting caused all observed recovery?
questions.questionText: What would weaken a claim that planting caused all observed recovery?
options: Several planted sites were monitored.
The same measurement method was used each month.
Plant survival was recorded as well as cover.
Unplanted reference sites recovered similarly during the same period.
questions.correctAnswer: Unplanted reference sites recovered similarly during the same period.
questions.explanation: Similar change without the treatment offers an alternative explanation.

questions.prompt: A forest's tree cover returns but nesting cavities remain scarce. Which claim is best supported?
questions.questionText: A forest's tree cover returns but nesting cavities remain scarce. Which claim is best supported?
options: Canopy cover guarantees every former nesting resource.
One habitat feature recovered while another remains limited.
The tree-cover data must be wrong.
Cavities cannot affect habitat recovery.
questions.correctAnswer: One habitat feature recovered while another remains limited.
questions.explanation: Structural habitat features can take different times to return.

questions.prompt: Site X retains 80 of 100 plants after a flood and reaches 85 after a year. Site Y retains 30 and reaches 90. Which statement matches the records?
questions.questionText: Site X retains 80 of 100 plants after a flood and reaches 85 after a year. Site Y retains 30 and reaches 90. Which statement matches the records?
options: X retained more initially; Y made the larger later gain.
Y retained more initially; X made the larger later gain.
Both had the same initial loss.
Both returned to their original counts.
questions.correctAnswer: X retained more initially; Y made the larger later gain.
questions.explanation: Initial retention is 80 versus 30; subsequent gains are 5 versus 60.

questions.prompt: A claim says recovery must end with the exact original species. Which evidence challenges it most directly?
questions.questionText: A claim says recovery must end with the exact original species. Which evidence challenges it most directly?
options: A single photo shows bare soil immediately afterward.
Long-term monitoring shows a different stable community under a changed water regime.
A few plants grow during the first month.
The baseline included several species.
questions.correctAnswer: Long-term monitoring shows a different stable community under a changed water regime.
questions.explanation: Persistent changed conditions can support a different community rather than exact return.

questions.prompt: A class doubles observation time after restoration and reports twice as many birds. What must be checked?
questions.questionText: A class doubles observation time after restoration and reports twice as many birds. What must be checked?
options: Whether bird names have changed.
Whether counts per equal observation time actually increased.
Whether total counts alone prove the habitat improved.
Whether observation time is irrelevant to sightings.
questions.correctAnswer: Whether counts per equal observation time actually increased.
questions.explanation: More effort can produce more sightings without a population change.

questions.prompt: A restoration plan includes native plants but overlooks continuing foot traffic. What model link should be added?
questions.questionText: A restoration plan includes native plants but overlooks continuing foot traffic. What model link should be added?
options: Repeated trampling -> damage to new growth -> slower establishment.
More trampling -> more photosynthesis in every seedling.
New plants -> no further need for soil.
Foot traffic -> guaranteed replacement of all missing species.
questions.correctAnswer: Repeated trampling -> damage to new growth -> slower establishment.
questions.explanation: An ongoing disturbance can counteract planting, so it belongs in the causal model.

questions.prompt: A site has regained plant cover and reduced erosion, but monitoring spans only one wet season. Which conclusion is most defensible?
questions.questionText: A site has regained plant cover and reduced erosion, but monitoring spans only one wet season. Which conclusion is most defensible?
options: Early recovery is promising; longer monitoring can test persistence through other conditions.
Every future dry season will show the same result.
The ecosystem is permanently restored in all respects.
Short-term improvements provide no useful information.
questions.correctAnswer: Early recovery is promising; longer monitoring can test persistence through other conditions.
questions.explanation: Evidence supports measured early gains, while long-term persistence remains untested.
